newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota crops need warm, dry weather.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota crops need warm, dry weather.

text.p: Cool, damp conditions aided Minnesota crops during the week ended Sunday, but warm, dry weather was needed now, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Average soybean height as of Sunday was 13 inches versus 13 a year ago and the five-year average of 14. Excess moisture in most areas slowed soybean growth and plants developed yellow foliage.

Corn height increased 10 inches over the week and reached an average of 43 inches, the same as a year ago but an inch shorter than average. Corn was rated 69 percent good excellent, 24 fair, five poor and two very poor. One percent of the corn was tasseling versus three last year and the eight percent average.
Soybeans were rated 51 percent good to excellent, 32 fair, 14 poor and three very poor. Ten percent were blooming versus 15 a year ago and the 24 average.

Spring wheat was two percent ripe and 77 headed versus five and 67, respectively, a year ago, and the 11 and 86 averages. The wheat was rated 45 percent good to excellent, 18 fair, 34 poor and three very poor.
Oats were 88 percent headed and 12 ripe versus 94 and 14, respectively, a year ago and the 93 and 28 averages.
Topsoil moisture was rated 22 percent surplus, 70 adequate, seven short and one very short.
